title: One cyclotron, many outputs: per-output rubrics, review, routing and monitoring
description: Acceptance test from the marketing-site diagram work (Cyclotron-web). Use case: one cyclotron with several outputs (classifiers) answering a checklist of questions about one item. Each output has its own rubric, labels, ML model and evaluation, and all are optimized against reviewer labels; supporting questions feed each output's ML model as features. The core works today (embedded_cyclotron.py:70-119, 336-345; batched_classification.py:22-44). The child issues cover the gaps found when walking the use case end to end.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Epic complete. One cyclotron now runs several reviewed outputs. Merged into develop:
- #9 flywheel29: sibling check at promotion. Each candidate is scored on its siblings' development labels, under a declared SiblingPolicy.
- #10 flywheelf5: seeded supporting questions.
- #11 flywheel19: shared supporting questions are asked once and paid once. This is a store flag fixed at creation, so existing stores keep their requests byte-for-byte.
- #12 flywheela80: per-output review-rate monitoring, plus Cyclotron.overview().
- #13 flywheel82: one review labels several outputs (checklists).
- #14 flywheel4b16: per-output review routing.
- #15 flywheelb2: deferred learning, with learn() and pending_learning().
- #16 flywheel52: promote a supporting question to a classifier of a new version.
- #17 flywheel6ff: estimated cost per output. Also fixed optimizer events leaking into sibling traces.
- #18 flywheel84: glossary terms in the console, docs and diagrams.
- #20 flywheel85: the weekly review estimate follows routing.
- #21 flywheela44: async optimizer transport. Deferred learning lends the store lock during provider calls, with supersede, cancel and fairness safeguards. learn() runs each output at most once per call.
- #22 flywheel6b: trace-ui control to promote a supporting question.
- flywheel07 and flywheela81 had already landed.
The CHANGELOG entry and the superseded/cancelled trace-ui outcomes are in the closing PR.
